chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is not correct for the Muslim woman to wear from the scarves and the gowns what does not cover anything.

key_terms.الدُّرُوعِ: Gowns or outer garments (plural of dir' or duri')
key_terms.الْخُمُرِ: Scarves or head coverings (plural of khimar)

ai.seo_question: What are the requirements for a Muslim woman's clothing during prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the minimum standard for a woman's prayer attire, ruling that garments must provide actual coverage rather than merely being present. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'satr' (covering) as a prerequisite for the validity of Salah, ensuring that the body is concealed from view during worship.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hamma, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It is not correct for the Muslim woman that she wears from the scarf and the gown what would not go round anything’.
en.sarwar: 14. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is not proper for a Muslim woman to wear of the veils and outer garment the kind that does not provide any covering.’”
